title: Uniqueness of list concatenation split
statement: Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be such that $n\mapsto n+f(n)$ is strictly increasing. If lists $x,u,y,v$ over a type $\alpha$ satisfy $|u|=f(|x|)$, $|v|=f(|y|)$, and $x$ concatenated with $u$ equals $y$ concatenated with $v$, then $x=y$ and $u=v$.
